title: Autofix agent: from GitHub issue to pull request

links.label: Agent PRs on the demo repo

tagline: A mini SWE-agent that turns a GitHub issue into a reviewed pull request: it reproduces the bug with a failing test in a Docker sandbox, fixes it, verifies the suite and opens the PR. It never merges.
problem: A model that edits code is only worth trusting when something other than the model proves the fix: a test that failed before the change, a suite that still passes after it, and a human review before anything merges.
built: A hand-written agent loop on the Claude Messages API (Claude Opus 5.5, no framework) with strict JSON-schema tools, prompt caching, context editing past 150k tokens, and hard caps on steps, cost and wall-clock time computed from real token usage. Given an issue URL it clones the repository into a fresh Docker container, installs dependencies, records a baseline test run, then cuts the container off from the network. The harness, not the model, enforces three phases: write a test that fails, only then change source, and submit is accepted only after the suite is re-run with no regressions, no existing test has lost lines, and the linter passes. The diff is copied out as a patch, committed on a fix/issue-N branch and opened as a PR with the root cause, before and after test output, token cost and a review checklist.
highlights: Live evaluation on six planted bugs: 6/6 fixed, 4 to 5 model turns each, $0.28 in total
Sandbox: non-root container with CPU, memory and process limits, network cut after install, no secrets inside, command denylist
The harness rejects any fix that weakens existing tests
Every API call and tool result logged to a JSONL trajectory with a static HTML viewer

The first live run exposed a real harness bug (a test written through a shell heredoc that the file tool never saw); the model reported the contradiction instead of gaming it, and that case is now a regression test
testing: A mock provider replays recorded trajectories, so the whole pipeline runs in CI without an API key, including the real Docker sandbox tests. In live runs the harness re-runs the target suite and rejects any regression before a PR is opened.
